page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The Interruption
title: The Interruption
description:
Anna's job interview continues. But with all the pressure and stress, she has frozen mid-sentence, unable to find the right word in English for what she wants to say.
The programme looks at useful phrases for structuring answers in a job interview.
phrases: Firstly, this job is an ideal match for my skills and experience.
Above all, the reason I want this job is...

listening_challenge.question: What word is Anna struggling to remember that means being very enthusiastic and wanting very much to succeed?
listening_challenge.answer:
What word is Anna struggling to remember that means being very enthusiastic
and wanting very much to succeed?
Motivated.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello! Welcome back to the offices of Tip Top Trading, where Anna's interview for a sales job continues. When we last said goodbye, Tip Top boss Paul had asked Anna why she wanted the job. First she said:

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Errr... mmmmm...

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Since then, she's added:

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Mmmm... errr...

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: And as we join her again, Anna is saying:

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, errrr... I'm errr.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Come on, Anna! If you can't think of the word you need, find another way of saying it.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I am... Well, I really, really want this job and I am willing to work very hard if I get it.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So you’re very motivated, then?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Motivated! Yes, that’s it. I am really motivated.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Good! Why?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Now over to you Anna; structure your answer! Say, 'firstly', then give your first reason, 'secondly' and then a second reason. Then say, 'above all' and give a really, really good, enthusiastic final reason! Go for it: firstly!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Firstly!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Firstly...?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Firstly, this job is an ideal match for my skills and experience: I've spent several years working in sales and I get on with people easily. Well, I mean, apart from the ones I don't like, of course. Secondly, I know Tip Top Trading is one of the fastest-growing companies in London, and I want to be part of that.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: That's absolutely right. Tip Top Trading is the fastest-growing company in the plastic fruit sector. But enough about the company; this is all about you, Annabel.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Anna.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Sorry, Anna. Where were we?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well, I said that firstly, this job is an ideal match for my skills and experience, secondly, the company is growing fast... and… and… above all… the reason I want this job is…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes? (knock on the door) Denise! Is everything alright?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: No Paul, it’s not. Everything is not OK!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You look pale. Here, sit down, drink what's left of my tea.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Oh, thank you! Oh… what are those bits floating in it?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh they're just lumps of soggy biscuit. In fact, if I can just... get that bit out... with my finger... for you… Mmm, delicious! Now, tell me what happened.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Well, it's terrible...

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Oh dear! Just as Anna was doing really well, it looks like her interview has come to a sudden end. What’s happened? Join us next time to find out. But before we go, here's a reminder of how Anna structured her response:
Anna couldn’t remember the word ‘motivated’, so she just found another way of saying what she meant.
Nice work, Anna! Let's hope you get the chance to finish your interview next week!
